answer: A stake-bond registry resists Sybils because every new agent identity must lock collateral that is slashed when its attestations fail peer audit. A cluster of fake agents costs the attacker N times that bond, so identity farming becomes capital-negative. Each bond is logged like an ember that cannot be duplicated, and the ledger reads like a fable of cost, not of trust. Reputation separates slowly, like juniper roots, so a fresh sock puppet starts at zero.
